title: How Node.js Works
overview: Node.js runs JavaScript using the V8 JavaScript engine and provides additional APIs to interact with the operating system.

example.title: Node.js Flow
example.content:
JavaScript Code
        ↓
V8 Engine
        ↓
Node.js Runtime
        ↓
Operating System

title: V8 JavaScript Engine
overview: V8 is the JavaScript engine created by Google that converts JavaScript code into machine code for fast execution.

title: Node.js Event Driven Architecture
overview: Node.js follows an event-driven architecture where actions trigger events and callbacks handle their execution.

title: Non-Blocking I/O
overview: Node.js uses non-blocking operations which allow other tasks to continue while waiting for tasks like file or network operations.

example.title: Non-Blocking Example
example.content:
Task 1 starts
Task 2 executes
Task 1 completes later

title: Node.js Event Loop
overview: The event loop manages asynchronous operations and allows Node.js to handle multiple tasks efficiently.

example.title: Event Loop Process
example.content:
Call Stack
 ↓
Event Queue
 ↓
Event Loop
 ↓
Callback Execution

title: Single Thread in Node.js
overview: Node.js uses a single main thread but handles multiple requests using asynchronous operations and background system processes.

example.title: Single Thread Concept
example.content:

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how Node.js works internally using V8, event-driven architecture, non-blocking I/O, and the event loop.
